title: The Earliest Time Two People Can Meet for a Given Length

concept.title: Sort both lists of slots and always move past the slot that ends first
body: Two people each give the time slots when they are free. The slots of one person never overlap. They want to meet for exactly `d` units of time, so the meeting `[x, x + d]` must lie **inside one slot of the first person and inside one slot of the second one**. Find the **earliest** possible `x`. For `d = 12`, the first person's slots `10-50, 60-120, 140-210` and the second one's `0-15, 60-70` give -1; for `d = 8` and the second one's slots `0-15, 60-100`, the earliest meeting is `60 68`.

The common free time of two slots is their **intersection**: from `max(s1, s2)` to `min(e1, e2)`. A meeting of the length `d` fits when `min(e1, e2) - max(s1, s2) >= d`. Sort both lists by the start; since the slots of one person do not overlap, they are also sorted by the end. Use two pointers `i` and `j`. Look at the slots `a[i]` and `b[j]`: if their intersection is long enough, it is the earliest possible meeting (all earlier intersections were too short, and later ones start later). Otherwise **drop the slot that ends first**, because it cannot intersect anything else in a useful way.

body.code:
a.sort(); b.sort()
i = j = 0
while i < n and j < m:
    lo = max(a[i][0], b[j][0])
    hi = min(a[i][1], b[j][1])
    if hi - lo >= d:
        print(lo, lo + d); break
    if a[i][1] < b[j][1]: i += 1       # the slot that ends first is finished
    else: j += 1
else:
    print(-1)

body: Each step advances one of the pointers, so the walk takes O(n + m) after the two sorts, O(n log n + m log m) in total. This "advance the one that ends first" rule is the same one used to intersect two sorted lists of ranges.

statement: Two people have lists of free slots `[s, e]`; the slots of one person do not overlap. They want to meet for `d` units of time inside a slot of each person. Print the earliest start `x` and the end `x + d` of such a meeting (two numbers), or -1 if they cannot meet.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, `m` and `d`: the number of free slots of the first person, of the second person, and the length of the meeting.
The next `n` lines have two numbers `s` and `e`: the free slots of the first person.
The next `m` lines have two numbers `s` and `e`: the free slots of the second person.
outputFormat: Print `x` and `x + d` separated by a space, or -1.
constraints: The slots of one person do not overlap (they are not necessarily sorted).

examples.note: The slots 60-120 and 60-100 intersect in 60-100: the meeting 60 68.
The intersections are 10-15 and 60-70, both shorter than 12: -1.

hints: Sort both lists by the start.
The common time of two slots is [max of starts, min of ends].
If the common time is too short, drop the slot that ends first.

explanation: Both lists are sorted by start; the two pointers compare the intersection of the current slots with the needed length and, if it is too short, skip the slot that ends first.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n + m log m), space O(1) extra.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m, d = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
b = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

a.sort()
b.sort()
i = j = 0
answer = "-1"
while i < n and j < m:
    lo = max(a[i][0], b[j][0])
    hi = min(a[i][1], b[j][1])
    if hi - lo >= d:
        answer = str(lo) + " " + str(lo + d)
        break
    if a[i][1] < b[j][1]:
        i += 1
    else:
        j += 1
print(answer)
